summary:
The design meets all three of ADV-C62H-2's conditions. I checked it against the code. Every explanation comes from a record the client does not write: the room's hs.server_hash, which is null only when the room coded that client nothing (room.rs:299-300 resets it; it is set only at :1128 and :1357), or npt-l1's fate, decided when the datagram is sent (l1/src/lib.rs:1097-1105). No client counter is read.

The closed list is complete for a correct npt-client on L1. The client files a tick lost only when the tick leaves its 32-tick ring unfiled (client/src/lib.rs:583-615). Decode failures file the sentinel instead (:717-807). Nothing newer is sent while a full state is in flight (room.rs:1087-1089), and no client ever sends Resync (grep finds none in client, bots or lab). A stale drop cannot happen on L1: the worst case is about 180 ms of link delay plus at most 33 ms until the client's next step, against the ring's 1,067 ms. Ticks the lab's stop decides lost never fall in a valid run's measured window (scenario.rs:1126-1130).

The join is exact. Only datagram() pushes Datagram fate entries (l1 :1107; stream entries at :1284, acks at :1438). L1 arms no probe timer while only datagrams are in flight (l1 :50-51). Pings and pongs go out only in io (scenario.rs:458-545). Client ends are never dropped mid-run. A too-large group cannot happen (room.rs:1172, :1337-1338).

The checks can fail on a broken lab and cannot pass on one:
- An overstated record fails the second figure.
- An understated record fails the first on every clean lossy run, at about 17,000 ticks a P2 run.
- A missing record is a gap, which makes the run INVALID (eval.rs:1215-1231).
- Both planted bugs are shown only when every one of their runs shows them (eval.rs:1489-1496).
- The new checks apply only to their own parts (eval.rs:1150-1152, :1452-1458), so P0 and the L2 parts never read the figures.

The size arithmetic holds (450 to 604 by file). The run time holds: 1,047 s plus 2 × 336 s plus 15 s for P2, plus 1,020 s for P3, about 46 minutes. The disk projections hold: 887.6 MiB and 524.4 MiB, so start checks at 4,983.6 MiB and 4,620.4 MiB free; 7,666 MiB is free today. No existing bar is reworded. The L1 P0 check gets one comma and nothing else. The order before U4f and U4g is sound.

Three Medium findings go into the text before it reaches Mustafa:
- The measured-window scope appears nowhere in the plain words, the check names or the README sentence. Figures take no window (marks.rs:547-549).
- A room tick record with no hs.server_hash list would count as "the room sent nothing", an explanation by absence.
- The paste must say how this design differs from option (a) as he chose it.

My answers to the design's five questions (C62HB-Q1 to Q5):
- Q1, leave "delivered too late" off the list: (a), yes.
- Q2, do the comparison in npt-judge as two figures: (a), yes.
- Q3, run the P2 planted bugs at full length in the judged set: (a), yes.
- Q4, keep -58's wrap parts out of this lane: (a) now. Offer them to Mustafa as a later decision once both sets PASS.
- Q5, JDG-ONLY-1's fix rides this lane: no, (b). It becomes its own change-set, so Mustafa's yes covers C62H-BOUND alone.

What I could not check: I ran no build, test or run (read only). The judged runs must still show 0 and 0 on clean runs, and the two planted bugs must each read 48. The test-engineer's read runs in parallel and is not folded in here.

findings.where: design plain_words; exact_texts.marks_json (both check names); exact_texts.readme sentence; crates/judge/src/marks.rs:547-549
findings.what: Both figures count measured tick records only. A figure check takes no window (marks.rs:547-549), so the JSON's only trace of that limit is the SERIES.md rows. The plain words ('every snapshot a test client files as lost ... zero of them on every run'), both check names ('every client-tick', 'no client-tick') and the README sentence ('a tick filed lost must have a reason') claim more than the figures compute: the warm-up and the after phase are not read. The plain words do not say exactly what the JSON computes, and his yes is on this wording.
findings.fix: Use 'measured' in the exact texts. Check 1's name: 'L1 P2, P3 and B1: every measured client-tick left incomplete is one the room sent that client nothing for, or one the link lost a snapshot datagram of (0 unexplained)'. Check 2's name: 'L1 P2, P3 and B1: no measured client-tick filed whole is one the link lost a snapshot datagram of (0; the link's record is not overstated)'. In the plain words, after 'files as "lost"', add: 'in each run's measured ten minutes (not its warm-up or its last few seconds)'. In the README: 'a measured tick filed lost must have a reason'.

findings.where: design judge: snap_lost_unexplained_count's room-side reader; SERIES row's gap list; crates/judge/src/figures.rs:236-279 and :400-404
findings.what: E1 is read through slot_hashes, where a room tick record that has no hs.server_hash list reads as null for every slot (figures.rs:249-276, :400-404). Null is E1, 'the room sent that client nothing', so a missing record would explain every tick filed lost at that tick. Today npt-lab always writes the list (logs.rs:564; npt-log set_hashes always inserts it, log/src/lib.rs:158-164), so clean runs are unaffected. But the bar's rule is 'explained only by a record', and absence is not a record: a later lab change that skipped the list on some ticks would let misfiled ticks pass there. The gap list covers a missing tick.s.snap_link_lost_count, but not a missing hs.server_hash.
findings.fix: Add 'a room tick record without hs.server_hash' to the figure's gaps, in the code and in the SERIES row's Gaps sentence. Add one engine.rs fixture: a room tick record with tick.s.snap_link_lost_count and no hs.server_hash, and an incomplete measured tick there, reads INVALID. About +5 lines.

findings.where: the paste to Mustafa (design questions C62HB-Q1, Q3; advisor-c62h-review-full.md:79-80)
findings.fix: Put a block titled 'How this differs from option (a) as you chose it' in the paste, beside the exact texts and the size: items (i) to (v), one line each. Also state what stays unbounded after it (-58's L1 P0 and L1 P3 wrap parts, -17's L2 parts, -17's L1 B1 until U4g). Also state that this is a stricter reading of ADR 0001's -17 row: the row is unchanged (sha256 3075f638…), his yes is the decision, and the readings PR lists it.

findings.where: design plain_words ('a client that files a received snapshot as lost'); crates/lab/src/logs.rs:317-331, :362-366; marks.json:4011
findings.what: The first planted bug sits in npt-lab's per-client log writer, not in npt-client. marks.json's own text calls it 'a client writer', and the advisor recorded that it proves the judge catches the outcome (advisor-c62h-review-full.md:37). The plain words make it sound like a bug in the client.
findings.fix: In the plain words, write: 'a planted bug in the lab's per-client log writer that files one snapshot per client, received whole, as lost, fails the first check (48 of 48 clients)'.

findings.what: SPLIT_LINE is a fixed text that says 'verdict.json holds the measured runs' verdicts (read its L1 P0 parts; ...)'. Once the P2 set has planted-bug runs, P2's runs.txt would print that wrong line. The design's expected lines for P2 say only 'the split line'.
findings.fix: In the runner edit (inside its +8 to 15 lines), make SPLIT_LINE name the set's profile, or no profile at all. Update the helper test with it, and show the P2 dry plan's split line before the set runs.

findings.what: Check 1 requires 0 datagrams sent for a slot with no session, but it allows non-empty groups there. Server::send drops such groups silently. If the room ever coded groups for a slot without a session, the tick would not fail where it happens. It would surface at the judge as an unexplained tick (the server hash is set, 0 recorded as lost), which reads as a client bug. Clean runs never do this: a closed link calls room.leave (:527-536), and a kicked client is skipped (room.rs:1047-1049).
findings.fix: Check 1 also returns Err when a slot without a session has non-empty groups. About 2 lines.

findings.where: design series_rows (3), the tick.s.snap_incomplete row's Marks cell (SERIES.md:320)
findings.what: The new cell '-17 (its L1 P0 check; snap_lost_unexplained_count), -58, -19 (the coverage rule)' reads as if the coverage rule served only -58 and -19. It also drops -17's report of the sum, which stays in marks.json. Today's cell covers both: '-17, -58, -19 (the coverage rule; -17 reports it)'.
findings.fix: The Marks cell reads: '-17 (the coverage rule, its L1 P0 check and its report; snap_lost_unexplained_count), -58, -19 (the coverage rule)'.

to_mustafa:
I have checked the netcode-architect's design for the limit you chose (C62H-BOUND (a)) against the code. It is sound and I approve it, with conditions. Most of them correct the wording before it comes to you.

What the limit does: on the lossy test networks, every snapshot a test client files as 'lost' needs a reason from a record the client does not write: the server sent it nothing, or the simulated network dropped a packet of it. Any other 'lost' snapshot fails the mark. A second check runs the other way: a snapshot the network dropped a packet of can never be filed as received whole. I traced every way the client can file a snapshot as lost. On the simulated network those two reasons are the only ones a correct client can produce.

What you should know beyond the design:
1. It differs from option (a) as you chose it, in five ways:
   - 'it arrived too late' is no longer an accepted reason. The bar gets stricter, because on the simulated network nothing can arrive that late.
   - It is two checks and two planted bugs, not one check.
   - The planted bugs run as full ten-minute runs inside the judged P2 set, not as one short run.
   - The runs take about 46 minutes, not about 35.
   - On B1 the checks only take effect when U4g's runs come.
2. It is stricter than the written pass mark in the netcode decision record (ADR 0001's row for -17). That row does not change. Your yes is the decision, and the readings pull request will list it.
3. Still unbounded after it: the same gap on -58's two wrap parts, -17's real-network (L2) parts, and B1 until U4g. The first can come to you as a decision once both sets pass.
4. The wording is locked by hash when you say yes. Any later change comes back to you before the judged runs. If any clean run, or even the build's own test, shows a 'lost' snapshot with no reason, the work stops and comes to you. The check is never reworded to fit.
5. The judge fix JDG-ONLY-1 gets its own small change, so your yes covers only this limit, about 530 changed lines. The build stops and tells you if it passes 1,050.
6. Today there is enough disk space for the runs (7.7 GiB free). If space is short by run day, the kept-logs packing goes first, after its own pull request to main.
7. The test-engineer's read runs in parallel. Its findings are ruled before the wording comes to you.

Decisions needed:
- C62H-BOUND-YES: Do you say yes to the limit's exact wording and its planned size? It is about 530 changed lines, and the build stops and tells you past 1,050.
  - Why it matters: nothing is built until you do. The wording is fixed from then on, and the judged runs can't reword it.
  - Options: (a) yes; (b) yes with changes you name; (c) no, and keep only the report lines that compare each run's count with the expected network loss.
  - My recommendation: (a), once the conditions above are applied to the text you receive.

For Mustafa:
1. Nothing yet. The exact wording comes to you after the fixes and the test-engineer's read are ruled; then answer C62H-BOUND-YES.
